detail.longDescription: The turtle moves to draw out a maze, in DFS it is not supposed to move to a place it has already gone to. I try to solve this by saving wherever it goes to in the 'visited' list, this works most of the time but sometimes it still goes in a loop and overlaps. You can run the code to see the problem, it keeps overlapping itself. I didn't add the part where it goes back a step if there are no more possible paths, but I will after fixing this problem. import turtle as t import random as r visited = [] def empty(pos): #checks if a position is not already visited or out of bounds x = pos[0] y = pos[1] if x < -100 or x > 100 or y < -100 or y > 100 or pos in visited: return False else: return True moves = 0 t.bgcolor("black") maze = t.Turtle() maze.color("white") maze.shape("square") #maze.hideturtle() maze.speed(1) maze.pencolor("white") maze.pensize(16) maze.penup() maze.goto(-100,-100) maze.pendown() while moves < 100: rotation = r.randint(1,3) if rotation == 1: maze.penup() maze.left(90) maze.forward(20) if empty(maze.pos()): visited.append(maze.pos()) maze.backward(20) maze.pendown() maze.forward(20) moves += 1 else: maze.penup() maze.backward(20) maze.left(-90) if rotation == 2: maze.penup() maze.forward(20) if empty(maze.pos()): visited.append(maze.pos()) maze.backward(20) maze.pendown() maze.forward(20) moves += 1 else: maze.penup() maze.backward(20) if rotation == 3: maze.penup() maze.right(90) maze.forward(20) if empty(maze.pos()): visited.append(maze.pos()) maze.backward(20) maze.pendown() maze.forward(20) moves += 1 else: maze.penup() maze.backward(20) maze.right(-90) print(visited) for i in range(0,99): print(empty(visited[i])) print("rep") print(len(visited) != len(set(visited))) t.done()
